paper.title: FLEX: Continuous Agent Evolution via Forward Learning from Experience
paper.central_claim: FLEX is a gradient-free learning paradigm in which a frozen LLM agent continuously evolves by building a structured, hierarchical experience library via actor-critic reflection on successes and failures; it yields large gains on AIME25/USPTO50k/ProteinGym, a 'scaling law' of experience, and plug-and-play 'experience inheritance' across agents.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; configured model type only

missing_sections: no appendix with prompts/hyperparameters (iteration limit, k for rejection sampling, updater prompt) present in material
figures are not in text (Fig 1,4,5,6,7 values only via captions/prose)

evidence.quote: delivers substantial improvements on mathematical reasoning, chemical retrosynthesis, and protein fitness prediction (up to 23% on AIME25, 10% on USPTO50k, and 14% on ProteinGym).
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim with maximum gains reported against the vanilla LLM.

evidence.quote: cultivates scalable and inheritable evolution by constructing a structured experience library through continual reflection on successes and failures during interaction with the environment.
evidence.support_explanation: States the retained non-weight object (structured experience library) and the reflection operation.

evidence.quote: (i) their evolving components are task-specific, thus they cannot generalize across tasks, limiting cross-task evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap with prompt/workflow/tool evolution; the three-part bottleneck is asserted without cited measurements.

evidence.quote: updater agent autonomously decides whether and how to incorporate it into the experience library.
evidence.support_explanation: Admission is delegated to an LLM updater; no measured-utility admission test.

evidence.quote: If semantically similar entries are found, the agent performs a selective merge, preserving the more informative or higher-quality trajectory while minimizing redundancy.
evidence.support_explanation: Dedupe/merge is the only stated maintenance operation; no forgetting, retirement, versioning or rollback.

evidence.quote: This process continues until the actor produces a correct or sufficiently improved reasoning trajectory, or a predefined iteration limit is reached.
evidence.support_explanation: Critic loop terminates on correctness (ground-truth) or an unspecified iteration limit; value of the limit not given.

evidence.quote: Retrieval proceeds hierarchically, the agent first identifies relevant high-level strategies, then locates corresponding procedural patterns, and finally accesses concrete case examples within each pattern.
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval is an agent-callable hierarchical tool (top-k, typically 5); this is how the stored change is read by later tasks.
Single-number accuracies LLM/ICL/Agent/FLEX; ICL is below vanilla here; AIME25 has 30 problems so one problem is 3.3 points; no variance reported.

evidence.quote: For AIME25, the training was conducted on 49 historical problems from AIME83 to AIME24. On GSM8k, we adhere to the official training and testing splits
evidence.support_explanation: Library is built on a disjoint training split and evaluated on a separate test set (structural construction/evaluation split); no contamination audit for AIME25.

evidence.quote: For USPTO50k, 100 instances are randomly sampled from the original 5k test split for evaluation, and 50 instances from the training split are randomly sampled for training.
evidence.support_explanation: Tiny train (50) and test (100) subsets; single random draw.

evidence.quote: shows a strong power-law relationship, with training accuracy increasing from 81.2% to 94.2% as the experience library grows from 1,001 to 1,904 items.
evidence.support_explanation: 'Power-law' is asserted over five epoch points; training accuracy is in-sample for the library's own source items.

evidence.quote: exhibits consistent improvement from 81.3% to 83.3%, significantly surpassing the 80.8% baseline.
evidence.support_explanation: Held-out gain across epochs is 2 points on GSM8k; 'significantly' not backed by a test; model in Fig 4 unnamed (80.8 matches GPT-3.5 in Table 1).

Only component ablation in the paper: exploration/evolution each add ~0.065-0.075 over no-tool baseline, together 0.573; regression tools alone give +0.059, so part of the ProteinGym headline is tool access.
Libraries built by another model lift the target above the ReAct baseline, indicating library content (not only own rollouts) carries gain; no random/shuffled-library control.

evidence.quote: is assumed to possess sufficient comprehension and reasoning capabilities to effectively utilize input information.
evidence.support_explanation: The 'theory' rests on assuming pi approximates the true conditional, which removes the KL term by assumption; Cor. 1 and Delta-I>0 follow from the objective definition rather than from a property of the update rule.

evidence.quote: These results demonstrate that our parameter-free paradigm can yield substantial gains in reasoning, an advancement previously achieved primarily through parameter-based learning methods
evidence.support_explanation: Compares implicitly to SFT/RL but no gradient-trained baseline is run.

evidence.quote: outperforms the baselines with the cost less than 100$ for both training and evaluation of a single agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Only cost statement: one aggregate dollar bound, no per-benchmark call counts or baseline-matched budget.

evidence.quote: ReasoningBank [ 121 ] scales memory retrieval at inference time without introducing an explicit learning process.
evidence.support_explanation: Closest neighbors (AgentKB, Memento, ReasoningBank, TF-GRPO, ACE, Reflexion) are dismissed in one line each and none is run as a baseline.

evidence.quote: Overall, these approaches do not establish a principled learning paradigm that formalizes how LLM agents can learn from experience in a continual, gradient-free manner.
evidence.support_explanation: Residual claimed over neighbors is 'principled paradigm' plus scientific-domain validation, i.e. formalism and domain rather than a measured failure of neighbors.

evidence.quote: a small experience set consisting of only 100 sequences (on average 1.47% of the available data), and a large out-of-distribution test set containing all remaining sequences.
evidence.support_explanation: Experience and test items come from the same protein targets (remaining mutations), so 'out-of-distribution' is a within-protein split.

evidence.quote: we reformulate protein fitness prediction as an agentic feature selection and fusion task, where the agent learns to identify, prioritize, and integrate salient features derived from existing regression-based models.
evidence.support_explanation: ProteinGym is a feature-fusion task over existing PLM scores with regression tools, not a zero-shot LLM task; gains mix tool use and experience.

evidence.quote: Semantic feedback distilled by the critic, evaluating both the reasoning process and outcome relative to
evidence.support_explanation: Critic sees the ground-truth label Y_i during training (privileged information at library-build time, not at test time).

evidence.quote: (2) LLM with In-Context Learning (ICL)
evidence.support_explanation: ICL baseline exemplars, number and source are not specified; no equal-compute sampling baseline (majority vote / best-of-N) is listed.

evidence.quote: The library structure is adapted to the benchmark: hierarchical for AIME25 and USPTO50k, and non-hierarchical for GSM8k and ProteinGym.
evidence.support_explanation: Library schema is chosen per benchmark; no ablation hierarchical vs flat.

evidence.quote: enabling LLM agents to continuously evolve through accumulated experience without gradient-based tuning.
evidence.support_explanation: 'Continuous' evolution claim; experiments are train-split epochs then a fixed-library test, not an online stream.

signatures.object: Hierarchical textual experience library (strategy / pattern / instance levels; golden and warning zones), a non-weight store; baseline = no library (LLM / ReAct)
signatures.information: Training queries with ground-truth labels visible to the critic (privileged at build time); test queries and labels not visible; ProteinGym uses cross-validation signal
signatures.operation: Actor rollouts (rejection sampling in parallel plus sequential critic-guided refinement) -> critic writes abstract task-agnostic suggestions -> updater LLM discards duplicates / merges similar / inserts by granularity
signatures.output: Updated library entries (success-derived golden, failure-derived warning)
signatures.conditions: Iteration ends on correct trajectory or unspecified limit; library structure varies per benchmark
signatures.feedback: Ground-truth correctness plus critic natural-language diagnosis
signatures.selection_rule_data: Training split only; LLM updater decides admission; no marginal-utility test, no held-out gate
signatures.persistence: Library persists across items and epochs and can be copied to other models
signatures.later_use: Agent calls library as a tool, hierarchical top-k (k about 5) retrieval at inference
signatures.claimed_effect: Held-out accuracy gains on AIME25, GSM8k, USPTO50k, ProteinGym; scaling with library size; cross-model inheritance
signatures.failure_boundary: No stated failures; no staleness/conflict handling; no reported harmful-entry analysis

signatures.object: Whole library as a transferable artifact across actor models
signatures.information: Library built by model A used by model B at test time
signatures.later_use: Retrieved as tool by target model
signatures.failure_boundary: Not tested across tasks or against shuffled/random library

gap.author_gap: Prompt/workflow/tool evolution is task-specific, not scalable with experience, and model-specific; prior experience methods lack a principled continual gradient-free paradigm and are validated on simple benchmarks.
gap.checked_gap: Real but narrow: a hierarchical, success-and-failure experience library with agent-tool retrieval validated on science tasks. The 'frozen weights' framing is background. The three named bottlenecks apply to prompt/workflow evolution but are not shown to apply to the closest memory/playbook neighbors, which already persist cross-task text stores.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion / Self-Refine -> Memento, AgentKB, ReasoningBank, ACE (playbook with curator edits) -> FLEX (adds golden/warning zones, 3-level hierarchy, agent-tool retrieval, ground-truth-validated build, scientific domains). Neighbor originals are not in the pinned input package; only the paper's one-line characterisations are available (v2 text).
gap.residue: Whether library content from labels beats equal-budget best-of-N or other memory schemes is unmeasured; cross-task evolution (named as bottleneck i) is not evaluated.
gap.stakes: Reuse of costly exploration across a model fleet; interpretability of learned guidance.
gap.method_response: Persistent hierarchical library with merge-based updates and cross-model transfer addresses scalability and model-specificity; cross-task generalisation is only asserted.
gap.remaining_gap: No comparison with the named closest neighbors; no cross-task or online-stream evaluation; no maintenance beyond dedupe/merge.
unresolved: Original text of ACE, ReasoningBank, Memento, AgentKB not pinned in the input package, so how far FLEX's update/retrieval differs from them (e.g. ACE delta edits) cannot be verified here; request in batch report.

claims.text: FLEX improves accuracy over vanilla LLM, ICL and ReAct on AIME25, GSM8k, USPTO50k, ProteinGym across 10+ models
claims.setting: Frozen models, ground-truth-supervised library build on small train split, library tool at test
claims.baseline_control: LLM, ICL (unspecified exemplars), ReAct without library
claims.selection_vs_test: Separate train/test splits; test not stated to guide selection except epoch tracking on GSM8k
claims.result_denominator: Single runs; AIME25 n=30, USPTO test n=100, GSM8k official test, ProteinGym remaining mutations per target; e.g. Claude-Sonnet-4 AIME25 40.0 / 50.0 / 63.3
claims.counterevidence: Baselines get no exploration budget; ProteinGym gains partly from regression tools (E013); ICL below vanilla on some rows
claims.allowed_conclusion: Library built from labeled training items raised held-out accuracy over single-attempt baselines in the tested settings; attribution to the library beyond extra exploration/tool access is not isolated.

claims.text: Performance scales predictably (scaling law) with experience-library size
claims.selection_vs_test: Training accuracy is in-sample; test accuracy 81.3 to 83.3
claims.result_denominator: Five points per curve; single run
claims.counterevidence: Library size and epoch are confounded; no fitted exponent or intervals
claims.allowed_conclusion: On GSM8k test accuracy rose about 2 points while the library doubled over 5 epochs; 'law' is not supported.

claims.text: Experience libraries are inheritable across agents (strong-to-weak distillation and weak-to-strong generality)
claims.baseline_control: ReAct agent of the target model
claims.counterevidence: No random/shuffled-library or ICL-with-same-source control; differences between sources are 1-5 points on n=30/100
claims.allowed_conclusion: In these tasks a library built by another model gave the target model higher held-out accuracy than ReAct without it.

claims.text: Gradient-free continuous agent evolution (a learning paradigm with theoretical justification)
claims.counterevidence: Evaluation is batch train-then-test, not an online stream; formal results are consequences of definitions and an assumption pi approximates p*
claims.allowed_conclusion: A train-then-freeze experience library; 'continuous' and 'principled' framing exceed the evidence.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A hierarchical text library built on a small labeled train split and used as a retrieval tool improved held-out accuracy of frozen LLMs over single-attempt LLM/ReAct baselines on four benchmarks, and libraries transferred across models on the same tasks; all author-reported single-run numbers.
unresolved: Whether gains survive equal-budget best-of-N and alternative memory schemes
No improver-level evidence (the update procedure itself is not shown to improve)

G.reason: Names a non-weight object (experience store) and cites task-/model-specificity of prompt/workflow evolution, but closest memory neighbors are dismissed in a line each without showing the residual bottleneck; value-add is largely framing plus domains.

M.reason: Actor-critic refinement, task-agnostic abstraction, zoned hierarchical library, tool retrieval form a reconstructible mechanism, but formalism does not generate distinguishing predictions versus plain retrieved-example ICL, and why the hierarchy/zones help is not argued.

X.reason: Operation chain described (explore, critic, update, retrieve) with ground-truth grounding, but iteration limit, k for sampling, updater prompt, forgetting/conflict handling, versioning/rollback and per-benchmark schema choices are unspecified; no failure/transfer boundary.

E.measurement.reason: Verifiable accuracy / Spearman metrics, but very small test sets (AIME25 n=30, USPTO n=100), unspecified ICL baseline, and no check that base models did not see AIME25.

E.causality.reason: Only a single-model ProteinGym ablation (which also shows tools contribute) and a cross-model swap; no budget-matched sampling baseline, no alternative memory scheme, no store-off with loop kept on math/chem, no gradient-trained comparison despite parameter-method claims.

E.holdout.reason: Train/test splits are separate for all four tasks and inheritance is on test items, but no contamination audit, GSM8k epoch tracking on test, within-protein 'OOD' split, and no cross-task holdout though cross-task evolution is claimed.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes stated but all main results are single numbers without intervals, seeds or variance; 'significantly' and 'power-law' asserted without tests.

E.cost.reason: One aggregate bound (<$100 per agent) in a figure caption; exploration/refinement rollouts vs single-attempt baselines are not budget-matched or itemised.

rationale: Experience-library system with held-out gains, but single-run small-n results, no budget-matched or neighbor-memory baselines; scaling law overreaches
